$comment: Europe in Motion. Each entry is a QUERY, not a banner: the fields below are evaluated against the Atlas on every build, and the resulting page states the query it ran in plain words. A motion whose query returns nothing fails the build rather than shipping an empty landing page. No motion may hand-pick destinations — there is no field for it, deliberately, because a curated list wearing the clothes of a query is the exact thing this refuses to be.

motions.name: Europe in autumn
motions.strapline: The shoulder, which is usually the better half of the year.
motions.lede: September to November is when the queues go, the light gets long and the food gets better. These are the places whose own quieter season falls in those months — not the ones that merely tolerate autumn.

motions.name: Europe by rail
motions.strapline: Where the train is the reason, not the transport.
motions.lede: Places we have tagged for slow travel by rail: reachable without flying, and worth the arriving. The Journey Planner will build a route through them with no flights in it.

motions.name: Europe's sacred places
motions.strapline: Cathedrals, monasteries, pilgrim roads and the quiet ones.
motions.lede: Fifteen hundred years of building for reasons other than commerce. Presented as heritage and as architecture, and open to anybody — the history is the point rather than the belief.

motions.name: Europe's hidden villages
motions.strapline: The small ones, computed rather than curated.
motions.lede: Everything here scores 80 or above for discoverability: not a capital, off the curated circuit, not tagged for the things a continent is famous for. The score and every term in it are published.

motions.name: Europe's islands
motions.strapline: Where the ferry timetable becomes the itinerary.
motions.lede: From the Aegean to the Atlantic. Islands change the arithmetic of a trip — fewer places, longer stays, and a boat that goes when it goes.

motions.name: Europe's mountains
motions.lede: Europe has more mountain range than its reputation suggests, and most of it is not the Alps. These are the places where the mountain is the reason to go.

motions.name: Europe's medieval world
motions.strapline: Walls, guildhalls, cloisters and streets that still bend.
motions.lede: Places carrying both history and architecture in our tagging — which is the closest honest proxy we have for a town whose medieval shape survived.

motions.name: Europe's culinary regions
motions.strapline: Where the region is the recipe.
motions.lede: Food and wine together, which in Europe usually means a place where what is grown, what is drunk and what is cooked all come from within about fifty kilometres.

motions.name: Europe under the northern lights
motions.strapline: Above 63° north, between September and March.
motions.lede: A genuinely geographic query: everywhere in the Atlas above 63° north. Whether you see the aurora on any given night is weather and solar activity, and nobody can promise it — what we can tell you is where the latitude makes it possible.

motions.name: Europe in winter
motions.strapline: Snow, thermal water, long nights and markets.
motions.lede: Places tagged for winter: skiing where there is skiing, but also thermal baths, Christmas markets and the northern towns that are better under snow than under sun.

motions.name: Europe after dark
motions.strapline: Music, opera, and the cities that stay up.
motions.lede: Places tagged for music and nightlife — which in Europe covers both a techno cellar in Berlin and an opera house in Parma, and the same list has to hold both.

motions.name: Europe's coastlines
motions.lede: Europe has more coast per square kilometre than any other continent, and almost none of it looks like the postcard. Atlantic, Mediterranean, Adriatic, Baltic, Aegean, Black Sea and Arctic.
